Subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Lina,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps to make sure we're aligned on deployment mode options (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) and the isolation concerns you raised.

Summary of what I heard from Acme Analytics:
- Primary use case: low-latency inference for customer-facing product features (personalized recommendations + short multi-turn chat).
- Expected peak: ~250 concurrent users, ~50 requests/sec during peak windows.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end < 150ms where possible; p99 < 500ms is desirable.
- Data sensitivity: not regulated but customer data is proprietary — prefer strong isolation.
- Main concern: "noisy neighbor" behavior from a shared multi-tenant pool that could cause tail latency spikes.

Deployment options we recommend to evaluate:
1) Hosted API (shared): fastest time-to-value; Redwood handles capacity and autoscaling. Good for experiments and unpredictable load but may see occasional noisy-neighbor tail effects under extreme contention.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): provides predictable throughput and isolation from other Redwood tenants. You get reserved throughput, configurable autoscaling, and SLA-backed latency/availability targets. Good middle ground for cost vs isolation.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: full network and tenancy isolation; best for highest security/isolation needs, but longer lead time and higher operating cost.

Questions to help us recommend the right default:
- Can you confirm the 50 req/s peak estimate and whether spikes (burst to 150 req/s) are possible for short windows?
- Do you have a strict SLO for p99 latency (e.g., must be < 1s)?
- Any regulatory or procurement constraints that would force Private VPC/on-prem?
- Would a capacity-based commitment (monthly reserved) be acceptable if it guarantees isolation?

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-FAQ.pdf (short FAQ on how Dedicated capacity works).

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm the numbers above, we'll put together an apples-to-apples cost + SLO comparison between Hosted vs Dedicated for your workload.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week with our SEs (Jonas and Dev) and your SRE to walk through traffic profile and isolation requirements.

Available times: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT or 2–4 PT. Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after discussing with the ops team: 

- The 50 req/s is the steady peak for our first phase, but we do see short bursts up to ~150 req/s for 30–90 seconds when promotions hit.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms is what the product team wants; p99 < 800ms would be a hard requirement for us (anything above that causes degraded UX).
- Isolation: we can't afford noisy-neighbor-related p99 regressions during peak — that alone is pushing us away from a shared pool unless we have documented and enforceable SLOs/fallbacks.
- Procurement: nothing forcing Private VPC today, but security will push for VPC peering and stronger network controls if we go beyond PoC.
- Cost sensitivity: we do have a budget target for Q3; Dedicated could fit if the unit economics are reasonable and we can scale down after initial months.

I've attached our network diagram and a short ops note (Acme-net-arch.pdf) to help your SEs.

Next step for us: we'd like a short technical session with your SEs + our SRE (I'll loop them in once you propose times). Can you include expected SLA numbers for Dedicated (p95/p99 and remedies) and an example noisy-neighbor mitigation playbook?

On Tue/Wed next week I can do Wed 11am PT.
